934:
Speed camera enforcement, using automated traffic enforcement safety device that is fixed is authorized within school zones in the city between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.
(Ord. No. 1129, 7-21-20)
935:
A. The city police, or agent on behalf of the city police, operating an automated traffic enforcement safety device provided for under O.C.G.A. § 40-14-18 shall maintain a log for the automated traffic enforcement safety device attesting to the performance of such device's self-test at least once every 30 days and the results of such self-test pertaining to the accuracy of the automated traffic enforcement safety device. Such log shall be admissible in any court proceeding for a violation issued pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 40-14-18.
B. The city police, or agent on behalf of the city police, shall perform an independent calibration test on the automated traffic enforcement safety device at least once every 12 months. The results of such calibration test shall be admissible in any court proceeding for a violation issued pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 40-14-18.
C. Prior to the placement of a device within a school zone, each school within whose school zone such automated traffic enforcement safety device is to be placed shall first apply for and secure a permit from the department of transportation for the use of such automated traffic enforcement safety device. Such permit shall be awarded based upon need. The department of transportation shall promulgate rules and regulations for the implementation of this paragraph.
D. For a period of 30 days after the first automated traffic enforcement safety device is introduced by the city police, or agent on behalf of the city police, within a school zone, the owner of a motor vehicle shall not be liable for a civil monetary penalty but shall be issued a civil warning for disregard or disobedience of the speed limit within the school zone.
(Ord. No. 1129, 7-21-20)
936:
Any person who shall violate any provision of this article shall be subject to the civil monetary penalties set forth in O.C.G.A. § 40-14-18(b)(l) as amended, including a fine in the amount of $75.00 for the first violation and $125.00 for the second or any subsequent violation, which shall be in addition to fees associated with the electronic processing of such civil monetary penalty, which shall not exceed $25.00.
Printed notices and/or citations shall notify drivers that they have been cited under O.C.G.A. § 40-14-18.
(Ord. No. 1129, 7-21-20)
937:
The following late fees shall be added to any civil monetary penalty not timely paid: (a) Thirty days after the due date printed on the second notice: $25.00; (b) Ninety days after the due date printed on the second notice: an additional $25.00. Total late fees shall not exceed $50.00 per violation and shall be printed on all notices.
(Ord. No. 1129, 7-21-20)
938:
Any person who desires to contest a notice of violation shall be allowed a hearing in municipal court for adjudication in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 40-14-18.
(Ord. No. 1129, 7-21-20)
941:
This article shall be known as the "Thomaston Personal Transportation Vehicle Ordinance."
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25)
942:
This article is adopted to address the interest of public safety. Personal transportation vehicles are not designed or manufactured to be used on public streets and the city in no way advocates their operation on the public streets within its jurisdiction. Adoption of this ordinance is not to be relied upon as a determination by the city that the operation of personal transportation vehicles is safe or advisable if done in accordance with this article. By regulating such operation, the city is merely addressing safety issues. All persons who operate or ride in a personal transportation vehicle on public roads do so with their own judgment and at their own risk, and must be observant of, and attentive to the safety of themselves and others, including their passengers, other motorists, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, the city has no liability in negligence, nuisance or under any other cause of action for losses resulting from the use or operation of personal transportation vehicles on streets under this article. Any person who operates a personal transportation vehicle is responsible for procuring appropriate insurance as may be required by any state law or this chapter as a condition of operating said personal transportation vehicle on the streets of the city.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25)
943:
For the purpose of this article, the following definitions shall apply, unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
Driver's license means a valid license to operate a motor vehicle issued by the State of Georgia or any other state.
Learner's permit means a valid learner's permit to operate a motor vehicle issued by the State of Georgia.
Map means the Thomaston Golf Cart Assess Map created by the city which depicts the designated streets within the incorporated boundaries of the city upon which the operation of golf carts is allowed.
Personal transportation vehicles or PTV means a motorized vehicle that:
(1) Is self-propelled by a motor engine, gas or electric;
(2) Shall have no fewer than four wheels;
(3) Shall possess an unladen weight of 1,375 pounds or less; and
(4) Shall not be capable of operating at a speed in excess of more than 20 miles per hour.
Such vehicles may also be traditionally referred to as "golf carts." The term does not include electric personal assistive mobility devices, power wheelchairs or scooters that can be used indoors and outdoors for the express purpose of enabling mobility for a person with a disability. The term also does not include any all-terrain vehicle, utility terrain vehicle, or multipurpose off-highway vehicle or other motorized conveyance designed for use on any surface other than a finished and paved surface.
Proof of insurance means written proof of liability insurance on the PTV insuring against personal injury and damage to property of any nature relative to the operation of a PTV on designated city streets in an amount not less than required by Georgia law for motor vehicles operated on public highways in the State of Georgia.
Sidewalk means a paved area of generally five feet in width or less that is designed or intended for the use of pedestrian traffic only.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25)
944:
(a) Registration deadline. The following registration deadlines shall apply:
(1) It shall be the duty of every owner of a PTV that is operated on city streets within the jurisdiction of the city to register the PTV.
(2) Registration following the implementation of this article, will be May 1, 2025. The initial registration will not expire until January 1, 2027, which shall be the deadline for the first renewal period. Thereafter, the registration for PTVs shall be renewed on an annual basis with January 1 being the deadline.
City council may, after the effective date of the ordinance codified in this article, alter the deadlines set forth herein above by resolution.
(b) Registration form and proof of ownership. The following provisions shall apply:
(1) Only those persons 18 years of age and older may register a PTV;
(2) PTV registration may be in one person's name only, and the registration form must be signed by that person;
(3) Any owner registering a PTV with the city agrees to abide by all of the requirements of state law and this Code. By registering a PTV with the city, the owner verifies that the vehicle qualifies to be classified as such under state law and this Code; and
(4) The owner shall complete a registration form, provided by the city, and take the registration form, together with proof of ownership which specifically sets forth the model, make, and any vehicle identification number or serial number on such PTV, to the city police department.
(c) Registration fee. The registration fee for a PTV shall be $15.00, and the registration shall be valid until January 1 of the following calendar year, except for the registration period beginning May 1, 2025 (see subsection (b) above). Renewal fees shall also be $15.00.
(d) Failure to register or renew. If registration is not made within ten business days of the date of purchase or there is a failure to renew the registration, a $5.00 penalty will be applied for each month the PTV remains unregistered. Said penalty shall be in addition to the late registration fee and shall not exceed $20.00. The late registration fee shall be $10.00.
(e) Waiver of registration. The city council may, at its discretion and by resolution, waive registration requirements for special events of a limited duration to which out-of-city residents may bring PTVs as participants. Such special events shall last no longer than three calendar days.
(f) Owner relocation. In the event a registered owner of a PTV changes his/her address or contact information after a PTV is registered, he/she shall have 30 days to provide their updated information to the city. Should an owner fail to comply with this provision, the PTV will be deemed unregistered and a penalty of $20.00 will be applied.
(g) Transfer of ownership. Should the ownership of a PTV be transferred to another person, the new owner must register the PTV in his/her name within ten business days of the change in ownership at a cost of $15.00. If the registration is not transferred within ten business days, it shall be considered an unregistered PTV and subject the new owner of such PTV to penalties set forth in section 86-139 below.
(h) Rentals. PTV dealers and distributors, along with other commercial establishments, may rent PTVs to the public for use on designated city streets. Each such establishment renting PTVs shall be required to register each PTV maintained in the establishment's inventory in accordance with this section and shall maintain a written record of each person who rents a PTV. Renters shall be required to furnish positive identification, shall be provided a copy of this article to read, and must be at least 18 years of age. The registration fee and transfer fees and regulations, along with all licensing and operation regulations shall be consistent with the provisions of this article as pertains to PTVs.
(i) License decal. Upon registration, each PTV shall be issued a license decal from the city signifying such registration, and a record of each license decal, together with the name and address of the owner, shall be maintained by the city. The decal must be affixed to the driver's side of the motorized cart in such a manner as to be visible at all times and shall remain permanently with such PTV unless the PTV is sold. The license decal is non-transferrable from the PTV for which it was obtained.
(j) Failure to display license decal. Failure to have a current registration license decal affixed to a PTV, as required herein above, for use on a city street shall be a violation of this article and subject the owner of such PTV to the penalties set forth in section 86-139 below.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25)
945:
(a) Required equipment for all PTVs.
(1) All PTVs shall have a braking system sufficient for the weight and passenger capacity of the vehicle including a parking brake, a reverse warning device functional at all times when the directional control is in the reverse position, a main power switch which shall render the power circuit inoperative when the switch is in the 'off' position or the key or other activating device is removed, such key or other activating device only being removable in the 'off' position, head lamps, reflex reflectors, tail lamps, a horn, a rearview mirror, safety warning labels, and hip restraints and hand holds.
(2) All PTVs operated on city streets must be maintained in safe conditions at all times.
(3) All gasoline-powered PTVs shall be maintained in such condition so that they are incapable of "backfiring", or otherwise operating so as to make loud noises; or create noise as a result of an operator equipping the gasoline-powered PTV with a certain device.
(b) Additional required equipment for gasoline powered PTVs. A gasoline powered PTV shall be equipped with factory installed safety systems, including indicator for gasoline or propane leaks, a speed governor and an exhaust system in good working order and in constant operation, meeting the following specifications:
(1) The exhaust system shall include the piping leading from the flange of the exhaust manifold to, and including, the muffler(s) and exhaust pipe(s).
(2) The exhaust system and its elements shall be securely fastened.
(3) The engine of every PTV shall be so equipped, adjusted and tuned, as to prevent the escape of excessive smoke or fumes.
(c) Additional required equipment for electric PTVs. Electric PTVs shall be equipped with, at a minimum, all factory installed safety systems and a charge indicator for low battery in good working order.
(d) Restrictions on changes to gasoline-powered PTVs. It shall be unlawful for the owner of any gasoline-powered PTV to operate or permit the operation of such gasoline-powered PTV on which any device controlling or abating atmospheric conditions, which is placed on the gasoline-powered PTV by the manufacturer, to render the device unserviceable by removal, alteration, or other interference with its operation.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25)
946:
(a) The city requires an inspection of all PTVs, for which registration is sought, to ensure that the PTV is equipped with all required equipment and that said equipment is in good working condition. Said inspection shall be performed by an officer appointed by the chief of police, and the inspection shall occur at the police department, unless an alternate location is mutually agreed to by the owner and inspecting officer. No license decal will be issued until the PTV passes said inspection.
(b) All PTVs shall be subject to inspection by city officials at other reasonable times and intervals, after the initial inspection. Failure to comply will subject the owner to the penalties set forth in section 86-139 below.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25)
947:
(a) PTVs may only be driven on designated public streets. A copy of the Thomaston Golf Cart Assess Map will be provided at the time of registration and each renewal, and the owner is required to maintain a copy of the map in the golf cart so that each and every operator of the golf cart is aware of the city streets on which golf carts are permitted and those city streets on which golf carts are prohibited.
(b) PTVs shall not be operated on sidewalks, within any portion of the public parks, or on any walking trails at any time.
(c) No PTV may cross any street, road or highway which is part of the state highway system.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25)
948:
(a) Those persons possessing a valid motor vehicle driver's license issued by the state, other state of the United States of America, or international agency which permits such person to operate a motor vehicle on the highways of the state may operate and drive a PTV on designated public streets.
(b) If there are requirements or limitations placed on a driver pursuant to state law, similar restrictions during the operation of a PTV shall apply.
(c) Persons who are 15 years of age or older who possess a valid instructional permit issued by the state, pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 40-5-24, as may be amended, and has not had his or her instructional permit suspended or revoked, shall be allowed to operate a PTV on designated city streets so long as he or she is accompanied by a person at least 21 years of age who holds a valid motor vehicle driver's license. Persons accompanying an operator possessing a valid instructional permit must be occupying the front seat of the PTV.
(d) No person under the age of 15 years shall be permitted to operate a PTV on designated public streets.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25; Ord. No. 1233, § 1, 4-15-25)
949:
PTVs may only be operated during daylight hours, meaning 30 minutes prior to sunrise until 30 minutes after sunset, provided that the PTV has all the required equipment and is operational as required by section 86-130.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25; Ord. No. 1233, § 1, 4-15-25)
950:
The number of occupants allowed in a PTV shall be limited to the number of persons for whom factory seating is installed and provided on said PTV. The operator and any occupants must be seated in the PTV at all times with no parts of their bodies extended outside the interior portion of the PTV.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25)
951:
All operators of PTVs shall abide by all traffic regulations applicable to vehicular traffic when using the designated public streets.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25)
952:
(a) The owner or operator of a PTV is liable for his or her own actions. Any person who operates or owns a PTV is responsible for procuring liability insurance and verifying coverage in terms sufficient to cover risk involved in using such PTV on designated public streets of the city.
(b) The owner and any operator of a PTV shall have written proof of insurance, and documentation of such coverage must be kept on the PTV or carried by the person operating the PTV.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25)
954:
(a) All violations of this article shall be charged by use of a uniform traffic citation and jurisdiction for the adjudication of guilt and sentencing shall be the city municipal court.
(b) Violations of state traffic laws and/or any other state law by the operator of a PTV while operating the PTV shall be subject to the same penalties which may be imposed upon the operator of an automobile under state law and shall be punished in accordance with section 1-11.
(c) Any violation of this article, excluding those violations referenced in subsection (b) above, shall be charged against the registered owner of the PTV as a municipal ordinance violation, and all fines and penalties shall be levied against the registered owner of the PTV as follows:
(1) For the first offense, a fine of not less than $250.00.
(2) For the second offense, a fine of not less than $500.00.
(3) For a third offense committed within one year of the conviction for a second offense for a PTV, a fine of $1,000.00 and the registered owner or his/her family member cannot thereafter register a PTV for use in the city for a period of two years following the third conviction.
(Ord. No. 1230, § 1, 4-1-25)

1133:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Taxicab means any motor-propelled vehicle operated over the streets or public places of the city for the purpose of carrying passengers for hire.
(Code 1965, § 30-1)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
1134:
This article is intended to apply to all taxicabs operated on or over any of the streets or public places of the city, regardless of whether the place of business or taxi depot or taxi stands of the owner or operator thereof are within or without the city.
(Code 1965, § 30-2)
1135:
It shall be unlawful for any person, either as principal, agent or employee, to use or operate or to cause to be operated upon any of the streets or public places of the city any taxicab without first complying with the provisions of this article.
(Code 1965, § 30-3)
1136:
Any person desiring to engage in the business of operating a taxicab in the city or to operate a taxicab therein, either as owner, lessee, operator or possessor in any right, shall, before operating, or allowing to be placed in operation any such taxicab on any street or public place of the city, comply with the following regulations and requirements:
(1) Application for license. Each such person shall file with the city clerk a written application for a license for each taxicab to be operated, stating the name of the applicant, his address and place of business. Such application shall also describe the taxicab to be used, shall state the make and motor number thereof, and the number of passengers such taxicab is capable of carrying. If such applicant proposes to operate more than one taxicab, he shall file separate applications for each taxicab.
(2) Insurance requirements. Each such applicant, at the time of filing an application for a license for the operation of a taxicab, shall file with the city clerk, for each taxicab proposed to be operated, a liability or indemnity insurance policy for injury to persons or property, in such amounts and containing such provisions as shall be approved by city council. Such policy or liability or indemnity insurance shall be in some liability or indemnity insurance company authorized to do business in the state. Such policy of liability insurance is intended to protect passengers in such taxicabs and the public against injury, against damage to property, and against injuries to person, whether fatal or nonfatal, caused by the operation of such taxicab, for which the owner or operator thereof may be liable under the laws of the state.
(3) Application approval; license fee; issuance. Upon the filing of such application and policy of liability insurance by an applicant for a license to operate a taxicab, the city clerk shall approve such application and insurance policy if they are in accordance with this article, but if not in accordance with this article, he shall return same to the applicant stating the reason for disapproval, in order that the applicant may correct whatever defect is necessary for approval. Upon approval of such application and policy of insurance, the applicant shall pay to the city clerk the license fee or occupation tax as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges for the period for which a license is sought, and thereupon the city clerk shall issue a license to such applicant.
(Code 1965, § 30-4)
1137:
Should such policy of insurance, as required by section 94-29 become void or ineffective at any time during the period for which a license may be issued, such licensee shall cease the operation of the taxicab covered by such policy until another policy of liability insurance covering the operation of such taxicab shall be filed with the city clerk.
(Code 1965, § 30-5)
1138:
The city reserves the right to revoke any license issued for the operation of a taxicab whenever the operator or the driver thereof is convicted of violating any provision of this article or other ordinance related to disturbing the peace or good order of the city.
(Code 1965, § 30-6)
1140:
No intoxicating liquor of any kind whatsoever may be transported at any time by any taxicab licensed by the city, or for which taxicab a license or permit has been issued by the city to any person whatsoever, nor shall any intoxicating liquor be within or upon such taxicab at any time whether such taxicab is moving or stationary. Nor shall any drugs or narcotics be transported by such taxicab except when transported pursuant to instructions of a licensed pharmacist. If it shall be made to appear to the satisfaction of the mayor and city council that this section is violated by the operator of any taxicab for which a license or permit has been issued by the city, then the mayor and city council may revoke the license or permit issued by it for the operation of such taxicab.
(Code 1965, § 30-8)
1144:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Bus carrier means every person owning, controlling, operating or managing any motor-propelled vehicle used in the transporting of persons on fixed schedule or from fixed termini, or over a prescribed route, other than permanent rail tracks, for hire on the public streets of the city.
Certificate means a certificate of public convenience and necessity issued under this article.
(Code 1965, § 30-9)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
1145:
This article shall not apply to taxicabs, drays and trucks operating on the streets of the city which do not operate on schedule, over a fixed route, or between fixed termini.
(Code 1965, § 30-10)
1146:
The city council is authorized to adopt such rules and orders as they may deem necessary in the enforcement of the provisions of this article.
(Code 1965, § 30-11)
1147:
Each bus carrier issued a permit of public convenience and necessity shall on beginning business, pay to the city a license fee as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges. Each bus carrier issued a permit under this article and operating in the city shall pay to the city a license fee annually in such amount as may be fixed by the city council, payable on January 1 of each calendar year.
(Code 1965, § 30-12)
1148:
All bus carriers carrying passengers for hire in the city shall have and maintain an office and agent in the city upon whom legal process may be served and submit to the jurisdiction of the courts of the county, upon all causes of action arising by reason of the operation of any bus within the city.
(Code 1965, § 30-13)
1149:
A bus carrier, having been granted a certificate of convenience and necessity, shall operate in the city such number of buses of a passenger capacity of not less than 16 persons as may be prescribed by the council when granting the certificate. Additional buses and routes may be required by the council when, in their opinion, the traffic requires such additional facilities.
(Code 1965, § 30-14)
1150:
(a) Any bus carrier, carrying passengers within the city for hire, shall prescribe just and reasonable rates, fares and charges for transportation.
(b) A schedule of charges for fares shall be filed with the city council, and this schedule may be reviewed and altered by the council after 60 days' notice to the carrier if it shall be made to appear that it is excessive or that the charges are inadequate to maintain the service, provided that if any one of the buses extend in travel beyond the city the carrier shall submit to the state public service commission regulation of its business beyond the city.
(Code 1965, § 30-15)
1151:
No bus carrier shall charge, demand, collect or receive a greater or less compensation for the transportation of passengers than the rates and charges approved by the city council, nor in any way discriminate between persons for service rendered with respect to charges.
(Code 1965, § 30-16)
1152:
Any bus carrier after having been granted a certificate of public convenience and necessity may discontinue its service after giving to the mayor 60 days' notice in writing and publishing such notice one time in the newspaper carrying the official advertisements for the city. The city council may cancel such certificate after a similar notice in writing.
(Code 1965, § 30-17)
1153:
The city council shall have the authority to promulgate rules designed or deemed necessary by such city council to govern the operation of buses in the city, and such rules shall include the following:
(1) Every motor unit and all parts thereof shall be maintained in a safe condition at all times, and the lights and brakes and equipment shall meet such safety requirements as the council shall from time to time promulgate.
(2) Every driver employed by a bus carrier shall have reached at least 21 years of age, shall be of temperate habits and good moral character and shall be fully competent to operate the motor vehicle under his charge.
(3) Accidents arising from or in connection with the operation of bus carriers shall be reported to the mayor.
(4) The council shall require and every bus carrier shall have attached to each unit or vehicle such distinctive marking or tags as shall be adopted by the council.
(Code 1965, § 30-18)
1156:
No bus carrier shall operate without first obtaining from the city council, after a hearing under this article, a certificate of public convenience and necessity pursuant to findings to the effect that the public interest requires such operation.
(Code 1965, § 30-19)
1157:
The city council may at any time, after 60 days' notice and opportunity to be heard and for good cause, suspend, revoke, alter or amend any certificate issued under this article, if it shall be made to appear that the holder of the certificate has willfully violated or refused to observe the conditions upon which the certificate was granted; any lawful or reasonable orders, rules or regulations prescribed by law; any of the provisions of this article or any other law of the city, this state or of the United States regulating the business carried on by the holder of such certificate; shall fail to pay any tax and license imposed upon such business in a lawful manner; or if it shall be made to appear that the holder of the certificate is not furnishing adequate service; or if the continuance of such certificate in its original form is incompatible with the public interest. If and when the city council shall undertake to revoke or modify any certificate on the ground of public interest being affected by the fact that traffic conditions do not justify the number of motor carriers operating within the city, the preference shall be given to holders of certificates in the order of the time of their issuance; other things being equal the junior certificates shall be cancelled first.
(Code 1965, § 30-20)
1158:
Any certificate described in section 94-77 may be transferred or hypothecated upon application to and approval by the city council and not otherwise.
(Code 1965, § 30-21)
1159:
The city council may from time to time in its discretion, without any new application or any hearing or any notice, renew and extend any certificate of public convenience and necessity issued at any time under the provisions of this article or any amendment thereto, and may issue in lieu thereof a new certificate of public convenience and necessity to the original holder, or his legal assigns, which new certificate shall be issued for such time and on such terms as the city council may in its discretion deem proper, and shall likewise be subject to the same privilege of renewal in the discretion of the city council as provided in this section.
(Code 1965, § 30-22)
1160:
In determining whether such certificate of public convenience and necessity, required by section 94-76 shall be granted, the council, among other things, shall consider the following:
(1) Whether existing transportation service of all kinds is adequate to meet the reasonable public needs.
(2) The volume of existing traffic over such route, and whether such traffic and that reasonably to be anticipated in the future can support already existing transportation agencies and also the applicant.
(3) Financial ability of the applicant to furnish adequate continuous and uninterrupted service for the year round; and to meet the financial obligations of the service which the carrier proposes to perform.
(4) The effect on existing transportation revenues and service of all kinds, and particularly whether the granting of such certificate will or may seriously impair essential existing public service.
(Code 1965, § 30-23)
1161:
(a) The city council shall adopt rules prescribing the manner and form in which bus carriers for hire shall apply for certificates required by this article. Until further provision is made the following shall govern:
(b) The application shall:
(1) Be in writing and under oath.
(2) Include a financial statement of the applicant and such information concerning the equipment proposed to be used as will enable the mayor and the city council to determine whether such equipment is adequate.
(3) State the proposed route over which the applicant desires to operate.
(4) Contain an agreement to submit a schedule for the operation of buses when required by the mayor.
(5) Set forth facts enabling the council to determine whether there is a need upon the part of the public for the proposed service.
(6) Contain such additional information as the city council may require.
(Code 1965, § 30-24)
1162:
The city council, upon the filing of a petition for certificate of convenience and necessity, shall fix a time and place for hearing the petition and shall give notice thereof by advertising the same at the expense of the applicant in the official newspaper one time six days in advance of the hearing.
(Code 1965, § 30-25)
1163:
No certificate required by section 94-76 shall be issued or continued in operation unless the holder shall give and maintain a bond or policy of indemnity insurance, substantially complying with the terms and provisions of O.C.G.A. § 46-7-12, which bond or policy of insurance shall be filed with the clerk of the city council.
(Code 1965, § 30-26)
1164:
A fee shall be charged for the issuance of every certificate and a fee shall be charged for the transfer of a certificate, which fees shall be as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges and paid to the city when the council shall have approved the application for the certificate or transfer. No certificate shall issue or be transferred as the case may be, until the fee shall have been paid.
(Code 1965, § 30-27)
1165:
Nothing in this article shall be construed to vest in the owner or holder or assignee of any certificate of public convenience and necessity any vested right to use the public streets of the city.
(Code 1965, § 30-28)
